newsitem.title: USA: Lexington Corporate to buy Hawaii store.
newsitem.headline: Lexington Corporate to buy Hawaii store.

text.p: Lexington Corporate Properties Inc, a real estate investment trust, said on Tuesday it entered into an agreement to acquire an 85,000 square foot department store in Honolulu, Hawaii, for undisclosed terms.
Lexington said it was issuing 225,000 partnership units convertible into common shares and assuming $8.3 million in debt, but that 207,741 of the units would not be distributed for another 10 years.
The transaction was expected to close during the next 60 days, subject to certain contingencies, the company said.

The property was leased to Liberty House Inc under a net lease which expired on September 30, 2009, subject to renewal options for another 26 years, Lexington said. It generated about $963,000 in net annual rent revenue, it said.
